source.title: Sheaf Discovery with Joint Computation Graph Pruning and Flexible Granularity
source.authors: Lei Yu; Jingcheng Niu; Zining Zhu; Xi Chen; Gerald Penn

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates IOI performance for circuits found by several methods and argues that a set of important components does not necessarily form a self-contained mechanism. It does not test the specific 26-head circuit from the original study.
record.gate_note: The IOI results in Tables 2 and 3 are included. Table 4's edge-representation cosine similarities are not IOI behavior measures; the reported composition and overlap results concern BLiMP, and results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: IOI is used as one benchmark task for comparing sheaf and circuit discovery methods (DiscoGP against ACDC, EAP, Edge Pruning and Weight Pruning) on GPT-2 small. The study never identifies, ablates or evaluates the Wang et al. 26-head circuit or its head classes. It does not compare circuit structure across methods (V4). It does not evaluate one fixed circuit under different ablations or metrics (V5). Each method's circuit is searched separately, and ACDC and EAP thresholds were tuned to roughly match DiscoGP's sparsity (Appendix C). The IOI numbers therefore measure method performance at a chosen sparsity, not how sensitive the IOI circuit's evaluation is.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that joint weight and edge pruning (DiscoGP) yields very sparse sheaves with near-full functional fidelity under zero ablation. They argue that collections of important components found by greedy methods do not always form self-contained mechanisms. They also argue that mean and interchange ablation are unsuitable because ablated components retain task information. Note that ACDC and EAP were evaluated at a sparsity budget matched to DiscoGP.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient-based joint weight and computation-edge pruning to find task-performing sheaves, and compares this with ACDC, EAP, edge pruning, and weight pruning. It does not identify or patch-test the original 26-head circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: For IOI, isolated accuracy differs across discovery methods (51.6% for ACDC versus 100% for Edge Pruning and DiscoGP). Mean-ablation results are also reported: ACDC-MA has 51.6% accuracy and DiscoGP-MA 100%.

fits_no_version.finding: At a sparsity matched to DiscoGP, ACDC and EAP IOI circuits reach near-chance accuracy in isolation (51.6%, 58.3%). Gradient-masking methods reach 98–100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuits from greedy importance-based discovery methods, at high sparsity, are not self-contained mechanisms that perform IOI in isolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean- and interchange-ablated edge representations keep high cosine similarity to clean ones on IOI (0.943 and 0.996, against 0.597 random). The authors argue these ablations leave task information in place.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mean and interchange ablation leave much task information in ablated components, so circuit fidelity under these ablations may overstate self-containment.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), 2024
record.problems: The IOI results are reported as averages of five runs without variability estimates. Only GPT-2 small is evaluated, and the study does not test the original named 26-head circuit.
record.rows_left_out: IOI weight and edge densities in Table 2 and Table 3 are not behavioral measures of the versions tested here. Table 4's edge-similarity measurements do not report IOI behavior.

untested.parts: All of it: the 26 heads, the seven classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality of the original circuit.
All of it: no name-mover ablation and no test of backup heads.
All of it: GPT-2 small only, no checkpoints, no reuse of IOI components.
Whether different methods recover the same circuit. Only fidelity at matched sparsity is compared; no structural overlap is reported for IOI.
No fixed IOI circuit is evaluated under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
Results are pooled over 15 templates; there are no per-template or name-order results.

missing.what: IOI cosine similarity between clean and ablated edge representations (mean 0.943, interchange 0.996, random 0.597). It bears on the ablation-choice debate, though it is not a behavioural measure.

record.verdict_notes: The record labelled the Table 2 and 3 rows as V5 support or limits. These rows compare different discovery methods' circuits at an author-chosen sparsity, not the IOI circuit under varied evaluation. ACDC accuracy is identical (51.6%) under zero and mean ablation, so the rows do not even show ablation dependence. The study is reclassified as T4 and its findings are recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: The specific 26 heads, seven classes, their roles under patching, and the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, and minimality are not evaluated.
No ablation of the original name-mover heads or test of backup-head takeover.
No other model sizes or checkpoints, and no test of component reuse across tasks.
The study compares discovery methods on IOI, but does not test whether they recover essentially the same circuit.
No per-prompt-format or per-template IOI results; the study does not establish that prompt distribution changes the evaluation.
Although the IOI dataset uses 15 templates, results are aggregated; the study does not test whether the same components carry IOI across prompt variants or more names.

relation.reason: The study uses the established IOI task and circuit-discovery framework to evaluate its own sheaves and method baselines; these comparisons do not directly test a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: IOI serves as a benchmark for discovery-method performance. The study does not evaluate the identified 26-head circuit, its head classes, backup mechanism, or structural recovery across methods.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 29 September 2025. Appendix C specifies comparable and larger sparsity budgets for ACDC/EAP, rather than exactly matched budgets; all listed rows remain method benchmarks with versions=none.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ACDC and EAP circuits under zero ablation; ACDC under mean ablation
reader_labels.reason: Their isolated IOI accuracy is 51.6%, 58.3%, and 51.6%, respectively, far below the authors' description of GPT-2's near-perfect IOI performance (R1, R2, R17).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Edge Pruning, Weight Pruning, and DiscoGP sheaves under zero ablation; DiscoGP under mean ablation
reader_labels.reason: These methods retain 98.4–100% IOI accuracy, so the incomplete performance is not uniform across discovery methods; DiscoGP-MA also reaches 100% (R3–R5, R16).
